q-44339.name: Question 1
q-44339.worked_solution:
First, we cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9k-5}{6} & =\frac{k}{2} \\ (9k-5)\cdot 2 & =6\cdot k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we proceed as usual to solve the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(9k-5)\cdot 2 & =6\cdot k \\ 18k-10 & =6k \\ 18k-10-18k & =6k-18k \\ -10 & =-12k \\ \frac{-10}{-12} & =\frac{-12k}{-12} \\ \frac{10}{12} & =k \\ \frac{5}{6} & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $k=\frac{5}{6}.$

q-101672.name: Question 2
q-101672.worked_solution:
First, we cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5k+2}{3} & =\frac{3}{2} \\ (5k+2)\cdot 2 & =3\cdot (3)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we proceed as usual to solve the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(5k+2)\cdot 2 & =3\cdot (3) \\ 10k+4 & =9 \\ 10k+4-4 & =9-4 \\ 10k & =5 \\ \frac{10k}{10} & =\frac{5}{10} \\ k & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-104488.name: Question 3
q-104488.worked_solution:
First, we cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{w-3}{7} & =\frac{1-2w}{6} \\ (w-3)\cdot 6 & =7\cdot (1-2w)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we proceed as usual to solve the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(w-3)\cdot 6 & =7\cdot (1-2w) \\ 6w-18 & =7-14w \\ 6w-18+14w & =7-14w+14w \\ 20w-18 & =7 \\ 20w-18+18 & =7+18 \\ 20w & =25 \\ \frac{20w}{20} & =\frac{25}{20} \\ w & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

q-171603.name: Question 6
q-171603.worked_solution:
We transfer the negative into the numerator of the fraction, and proceed with cross-multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{y+5}{3} & =\frac{4y+3}{5} \\ \frac{-(y+5)}{3} & =\frac{4y+3}{5} \\ \frac{-y-5}{3} & =\frac{4y+3}{5} \\ (-y-5)\cdot 5 & =3\cdot (4y+3)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we proceed as usual to solve the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-y-5)\cdot 5 & =3\cdot (4y+3) \\ -5y-25 & =12y+9 \\ -5y-25+5y & =12y+9+5y \\ -25 & =17y+9 \\ -25-9 & =17y+9-9 \\ -34 & =17y \\ \frac{-34}{17} & =\frac{17y}{17} \\ -2 & =y\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $y=-2.$
